newsitem.title: THAILAND: Norway PM rallies support for Burma sanctions-paper.
newsitem.headline: Norway PM rallies support for Burma sanctions-paper.

text.p: Norway is seeking international support for sanctions against Burma, visiting Prime Minister Gro Harlem Brundtland said in a newspaper interview.
She also crticised the seven-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations' (ASEAN) policy of constructive engagement with the military government in Burma and said it had produced no results so far.
"The situation in Burma is such that one should have a stronger common policy of trying to stimulate change," she told the Bangkok Post newspaper in an interview published on Tuesday.

"We have not up to now seen a general agreement in the international society about carrying out a sanctions policy (against Burma). It is only when you have a broad agreement on a certain policy that it works."
On the ASEAN dialogue with Burma, she said: "We are impatient about the lack of results so far."
Norway has been critical of the lack of democracy in Burma and use of forced child labour.

But it has become more vocal since its honorary consul and a long-time friend of Burmese democracy leader Aung San Suu Kyi, James Leander Nichols, died while serving a prison term in Rangoon in June after being charged with illegal possession of fax machines.
Burmese authorities said Nichols died of heart problems, but Norway and other European nations for whom he was consul in Burma have sought a clarification from Rangoon.
"The death of Mr Nichols was a very bad signal, one example of several things that should not have happened," Brundtland said.
She also called on Thailand to urge ASEAN to review its ongoing dialogue with Burma and not to rush into accepting Rangoon as a new member of the regional group.
Burma has asked for entry into the group next year, but ASEAN is divided on the timing of its entry, with some seeking political and human rights changes in the country.
In addition, they want a more meaningful dialogue between the ruling State Law and Order Restoration Council and Suu Kyi as a precondition for entry.
